title: Bagging, boosting, and a feature score
summary: Random forests, AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost, and what an importance number is.

choices.text: Boosting fits many trees at the same time on bootstrap samples and averages them, which is why it mainly lowers variance rather than bias.

Bagging trains each model on a bootstrap sample and averages them. A random forest is bagged trees that also try only a random subset of features at each split, which lowers variance against one deep tree.
AdaBoost fits its weak learners in parallel on reweighted copies of the data and averages them with equal votes, so a more accurate learner gets no extra say.
Gradient boosting adds models in sequence, each fit to the negative gradient of the ensemble's loss. For squared error that target is the residual.
XGBoost differs from gradient boosting mainly in training each tree on a bootstrap sample, as a random forest does, and that sampling is where its regularization comes from.

Mean decrease in impurity tends to favor features with more candidate split points. Permutation importance (the drop in a held-out score when a column is shuffled) is the fairer check, and neither number is a causal effect.
On a small table whose signal is close to linear, a tree ensemble cannot overfit, because averaging many trees cancels their variance, so a linear baseline adds nothing.
